source_text: ὡδί πη πάλιν· «Καὶ ταῦτα φάγεσθε ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν ἐν τοῖς ὕδασι· πάντα ὅσα ἐστὶν αὐτοῖς πτερύγια καὶ λεπίδες ἐν τοῖς ὕδασι, καὶ ἐν ταῖς θαλάσσαις, καὶ ἐν τοῖς χειμάῤῥοις, ταῦτα φάγεσθε· καὶ πάντα ὅσα οὐκ ἔστιν αὐτοῖς πτερύγια, οὔτε λεπίδες ἐν τοῖς ὕδασι, καὶ ἐν ταῖς θαλάσσαις, καὶ ἐν τοῖς χειμάῤῥοις, ἀπὸ πάντων ὧν ἐρεύγεται τὰ ὕδατα καὶ ἀπὸ πάσης ψυχῆς ζώσης ἐν τῷ ὕδατι, βδέλυγμά ἐστι, καὶ βδελύγματα ἔσονται ὑμῖν. Ἀπὸ τῶν κρεῶν αὐτῶν οὐκ ἔδεσθε, καὶ τὰ θνησιμαῖα αὐτῶν βδελύξεσθε, καὶ πάντα ὅσα οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν αὐτοῖς πτε
pass_a_gloss: §21 dual gloss: πτερύγιον / fins · λεπίς / scales · βδέλυγμα / abomination … Pass A ≠ Pass B. Theme: Fish with fins/scales vs mud-dwellers; world-sea begins.
pass_b_english: Cyril: ...thus somehow again: 'And these you will eat from all the in the waters; all as many as there are for them fins and scales in the waters, and in the seas, and in the torrents, these you will eat; and all as many as there are not for them fins, nor scales in the waters, and in the seas, and in the torrents, from all which the waters belch-up and from every living soul in the water, an abomination it is, and abominations they will be for you. From their fleshes you will not eat, and their carcasses you will abominate, and all as many as there are not in them fins nor scales of the in the waters, an abomination this is for you.' (Leviticus 11:9–12)
Palladius: But what ever is at least in these the difference, according to contemplation at least I say the spiritual, you yourself would speak. For I understand not somehow very much.

Cyril: Very much so; for I will speak, as possible, reshaping unto the apparent the as in a manner of examples having been taken-beside by the law; for as many as of the in the waters have been well-formed by the Craftsman of all according to the law of the fishes, as it were always rowing-through with the castings of the fins, they make the movement which they would somehow choose as well-strong and most well-running. And with sun casting from above into the waters the approach of the ray, they swim-up, and all but also dare to leap-up from the waters themselves, refusing to remain always below, and they go-through easily also the nets of those hunting. And those at least not being in scales and fins, or being in hard shells, and having been clothed with the connatural shell, least know the above, and they always sink-in the grass unto the below, and love-to-dwell in the muddy of the places. And they are strengthless and easy-to-catch, and for those having seen them once, takeable without sweat. And a word at least upon those, this, both clear and true; and let us go again as from images and types unto the more apparent.
Palladius: You would speak most excellently, and toward this at least going eagerly.
Cyril: The distraction of this life
